rationale: B wins by a slight margin because it finds a fourth real protagonist: "The brands get paid on day one. Faire waits 60 days for the money." A is disciplined, but "A wholesale marketplace becomes a bank" mostly re-dresses the same balance-sheet-risk story it already told. B still needs a red pen on "eat the credit risk itself"; that is a conclusion sitting where an unanswered disclosure question belongs.
gaps_in_A: "A wholesale marketplace becomes a bank" is too theatrical and overlaps with "Faire, valued at $12.6B, quietly becomes a lender to its own marketplace"; it needs real marketplace or embedded-credit comparators before it becomes a separate story.
"Independent retailers say cash flow, not demand" adds "not demand" without support; the update only says cash flow is the top barrier.
It leaves the supplier-side story on the table; "brands are paid upfront while retailers pay later" deserves its own brand/trade angle, not just a proof point.
"quietly becomes" is unsupported tone. No fact says Faire hid or soft-launched this.
gaps_in_B: "eat the credit risk itself" and "out of its own pocket" assert the financing source and loss bearer even though default-rate and financing-cost terms are not disclosed.
"That makes a marketplace into a lender to 700,000 shops" implies universal eligibility or usage; 700,000 is the total retailer base, not the launch population.
"ahead of whatever buying season the brands are working toward" is a fake peg with a hat on. No buying-season fact was supplied.
"retailers aren't ordering less because they expect fewer customers" repeats the unsupported demand leap; cash flow being the top barrier does not prove demand is healthy.
